description:
Episode 32 of a daily journey through the universe. ❄️
We visit Mercury: the smallest planet, 430°C days and −180°C nights, ice hiding in shadowed polar craters, an 88-day year, and a planet that is slowly shrinking.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 33: Next stop, tonight's shooting stars: the Geminids.

segments.text: Mercury is the smallest planet, and the closest to the Sun.
segments.headline: The smallest planet

segments.text: Days reach about four hundred thirty degrees Celsius. Nights drop to minus one hundred eighty.
Yet there's ice on Mercury, hidden in craters near its poles, where sunlight never reaches.
segments.headline: Ice near the Sun?

segments.text: A year on Mercury lasts just eighty-eight Earth days.
And it's shrinking. As its iron core cools, the whole planet slowly contracts, wrinkling its surface.
segments.headline: A shrinking planet

segments.text: Tomorrow night, look up: the best meteor shower of the year peaks. Next stop: the Geminids. Follow, so you don't miss episode thirty-three.
